42862276.label: Purpose
42862276.text: Intracranial space-occupying lesions (SOL), including primary brain tumors, metastases, and inflammatory lesions, require accurate characterization for diagnosis and management. Although ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT reflects tumor glucose metabolism, its performance in the brain is limited by high physiological uptake. ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT targets fibroblast activation protein in the tumor microenvironment and may provide complementary biological information with improved lesion conspicuity. This study aimed to compare ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI and ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT for the evaluation of intracranial SOL.

42862276.label: Methods
42862276.text: Thirty-five patients with 55 intracranial lesions underwent paired ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI and ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT within a 7-day interval. Imaging findings were compared with histopathology (n = 9) and/or MRI (n = 46) as reference standards. Lesion detection rate, diagnostic performance, tumor-to-background ratio (TBR), and semi-quantitative uptake parameters normalized to lean body mass (SUL) were evaluated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed to assess the ability of each tracer to differentiate neoplastic from non-neoplastic lesions.

42862276.label: Results
42862276.text: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT detected more lesions than ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT (48/55, 87.3% vs. 36/55, 65.5%) and approached the detection rate of MRI (54/55, 98.2%). FAPI demonstrated higher sensitivity and accuracy, whereas FDG showed higher specificity. FAPI demonstrated a significantly higher tumor-to-background ratio (TBR) than FDG (median, 342.00 [IQR, 164.25-502.00] vs. 4.71 [IQR, 3.48-7.42]; Z = 5.07, p < 0.001) in paired analysis of 34 lesions with measurable uptake on both tracers. In primary tumors, FAPI detected all lesions (13/13), whereas FDG detected 9/13 lesions. ROC analysis showed comparable diagnostic performance for differentiating neoplastic from non-neoplastic lesions (AUC 0.794 for FAPI vs. 0.796 for FDG). Exploratory analysis in high-grade tumors (n = 5) suggested a potential association between higher FDG uptake and shorter overall survival.

42862276.label: Conclusion
42862276.text: In this cohort, intracranial lesions were predominantly metastatic, with MRI showing the highest detection rate. Compared with ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT, ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated higher lesion detection and tumor-to-background contrast, approaching MRI performance. These findings support a complementary role for ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT alongside MRI and ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT in selected intracranial lesions, particularly when lesion conspicuity is limited by the high physiological brain uptake of FDG.

42867376.text: Background The grading system for invasive lung adenocarcinoma proposed by the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) has been widely validated. However, the association of PET/CT with IASLC grade and its value in clinical decision-making is unknown. Purpose To investigate the association of PET/CT metabolic parameters with IASLC grade and determine the complementary clinical value of PET/CT in optimizing preoperative surgical decision-making in clinical stage IA (cIA) lung adenocarcinoma. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent preoperative PET/CT and complete resection for cIA lung adenocarcinoma between September 2020 and March 2022. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma. Multivariable Cox models assessed prognostic effects and interactions between maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and surgical strategy. Propensity score matching was used to balance clinicopathologic characteristics across surgical strategies. Results The study included 2789 patients (median age, 62 years [IQR, 55-68 years]; 1574 women). Logistic regression analysis demonstrated a positive interaction between radiologic type and SUVmax (P = .008) in predicting grade 3 adenocarcinoma. Specific cutoff values for pure solid (cutoff of 4.25) and subsolid (cutoff of 2.30) nodules were identified. Positive interactions between SUVmax and surgery were observed exclusively in pure solid nodules (SUVmax-resection extent for overall survival [OS], P = .048; SUVmax-nodal dissection for OS, P = .045). Stratified analyses showed that segmentectomy and limited lymph node dissection were associated with worse outcomes only in hypermetabolic lesions (SUVmax > 4.25; resection extent hazard ratio [HR] for OS, 2.06 [P = .03]; nodal dissection HR for OS, 2.06 [P = .005]). SUVmax maintained robust predictive efficacy for grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma in the external cohort (area under the receiver operating curve, 0.72 for pure solid nodules and 0.74 for subsolid nodules). Conclusion In patients who underwent PET/CT and complete resection for clinical stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, maximum standardized uptake value was an independent predictor of grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma and helped identify high-risk patients treated with segmentectomy or limited nodal dissection.

42912576.text: A woman in her 50s receiving paclitaxel, carboplatin, and pembrolizumab for recurrent cervical cancer developed herpes zoster and received antiviral therapy. 18 F-FDG PET/CT performed 22 days after zoster onset, when the skin lesions had crusted, demonstrated continuous uptake extending from the left L5 dorsal root ganglion to the sciatic nerve. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of FDG PET findings indicating ganglioneuritis extending from the dorsal root ganglion to a peripheral nerve after herpes zoster. Recognition of this pattern is important in patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy because it may mimic immune-related neuritis or perineural tumor spread.

43002576.text: An 86-year-old man underwent radical prostatectomy for prostate adenocarcinoma (T3aN0M0) 5 years ago. He presented with recurrent constipation for 5 months. Pelvic MRI raised suspicion of rectal cancer. Serum prostate specific antigen (PSA) was mildly elevated (9.610 ng/mL). PET/CT revealed thickened rectal walls with no significant hypermetabolism on 18F‑FDG imaging, but marked radiotracer uptake on 68Ga‑PSMA imaging (SUVmax = 22.4). Final pathology confirmed metastatic prostate cancer to the rectum. For patients with a history of prostate cancer presenting with rectal occupying lesions, metastatic disease should be included in the differential diagnosis.

43016126.label: Objectives
43016126.text: Determining the probability of malignancy of a breast lesion allows for the appropriate triage of follow-up. Although BI-RADS provides standardized risk stratification for mammography, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging, no equivalent classification system exists for breast elastography. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a data-driven E-BI-RADS classification for breast elastography and to compare its diagnostic performance with B-mode BI-RADS.

43016126.label: Materials and methods
43016126.text: In this retrospective study, consecutive patients undergoing breast imaging with available B-mode ultrasound, shear-wave elastography (SWE), and strain elastography (10L4 transducer, Siemens ACUSON Sequoia) from 06/2023 to 12/2025 were included. A multivariable logistic regression model combining SWE velocity and elastography-to-B-mode lesion size (E/B) ratio was used to estimate malignancy probability, followed by Platt recalibration. Data-driven probability cutoffs were derived to define E-BI-RADS categories aligned with the BI-RADS concept. (E-)BI-RADS categories 4 and 5 were considered an indication for biopsy. Histopathologic evaluation or imaging follow-up served as the reference standard.

43016126.label: Results
43016126.text: The cohort comprised 344 breast lesions in 337 patients, including 224 (65.1%) malignant and 120 (34.9%) benign lesions. B-mode BI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 98.6% (221/224) and a specificity of 34.2% (41/120). E-BI-RADS demonstrated malignancy rates of 0.0% in E-BI-RADS 2 (0/71); 5.3% in E-BI-RADS 3 (1/19); 85.2% in E-BI-RADS 4 (155/182); and 94.4% in E-BI-RADS 5 (68/70). E-BI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 99.6% (223/224) and a specificity of 74.2% (89/120). The single false-negative case was a 31 mm B-cell lymphoma, classified as E-BI-RADS 3, with a shear-wave velocity of 4.4 m/s and an E/B ratio of 0.9. Decision-curve analysis demonstrates that E-BI-RADS achieves higher net benefit than SWE-based and B-mode BI-RADS strategies.

43016126.label: Discussion
43016126.text: E-BI-RADS provides the first standardized, BI-RADS-like classification system for breast elastography and enables safe biopsy de-escalation with excellent sensitivity and improved specificity compared with existing approaches.

43019576.text: A 9-year-old boy with neuroblastoma was enrolled in a clinical trial. After radiotherapy to the primary tumor site, 18F-MFBG PET/CT was performed 2 months later. No abnormal radiotracer accumulation suggestive of metastatic disease was identified. However, focal intense 18F-MFBG uptake was observed in the upper pole of the left kidney, within the previously irradiated field. No structural renal lesion was identified on cross-sectional imaging, and no evidence of renal tumor was found during 12 months of clinical and imaging follow-up. This case illustrates that intense localized renal 18F-MFBG uptake may result from radiation and should be recognized as a potential pitfall in post-radiotherapy 18F-MFBG PET/CT interpretation.

43056276.text: Female infertility affects approximately 15% of couples of reproductive age, with tubal disease responsible for up to one-third of cases. Therefore, accurate, minimally invasive evaluation of tubal patency is a cornerstone of fertility assessment. Among the available modalities, including hysterosalpingography (HSG), MR HSG, and laparoscopic chromopertubation, hysterosalpingo-contrast sonography (HyCoSy) has gained prominence as a valuable alternative to conventional methods due to its safety, accessibility, and diagnostic reliability. Recent advances in contrast-enhanced US involving the use of second-generation microbubble agents combined with three-dimensional (3D) and four-dimensional (4D) acquisition technologies have significantly improved the performance of HyCoSy. These developments enable real-time volumetric visualization of the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes, enhancing both anatomic delineation and functional assessment of tubal patency. In addition, combined 3D and 4D (3D-4D) HyCoSy enables complementary evaluation of uterine morphology, adnexal structures, and associated infertility-related disorders such as endometriosis and adhesions, facilitating a comprehensive "one-stop" reproductive imaging approach. This article is intended to serve as a practical guide to performing 3D-4D HyCoSy with microbubble contrast agents, including preparation, technical parameters, and findings interpretation. In addition, the authors compare HyCoSy with conventional techniques, review characteristic imaging patterns of tubal patency and occlusion, and discuss potential pitfalls and preventive strategies. As an advanced US technology combined with a dynamic functional perspective, 3D-4D HyCoSy represents a powerful, cost-effective, and patient-friendly tool for integrated fertility evaluation in modern radiology practices.

43058376.label: Background
43058376.text: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted imaging using 68Ga or 18F has been applied in differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), especially in postoperative follow-up, but its application value in the preoperative period remains largely unknown. This study aimed to prospectively evaluate the diagnostic value of [18F] -FAPI PET/CT for primary papillary thyroid carcinoma and cervical lymph node metastasis (LNM), and explore the association between the quantitative metabolic parameters of primary lesions and LNM.

43058376.label: Results
43058376.text: In total, 43 participants (median age 50 years) with 58 thyroid lesions (45 papillary thyroid carcinoma and 13 benign lesions) were included. [18F]-FAPI PET/CT and US had comparable diagnostic accuracy for primary thyroid lesions (P>0.05). For 23 cervical regional LNM sites, 18F-FAPI imaging outperformed US, showing substantial consistency with pathological results (κ = 0.603, P<0.001) versus moderate consistency observed for US (κ = 0.385, P = 0.002). The proportion of ipsilateral cervical LNM was higher in [18F]-FAPI-positive thyroid lesions than negative lesions (60% vs. 20%, P = 0.035). The LNM-positive group exhibited higher FTV (FAP expression tumor volume) (P = 0.004) and TLF (total lesion FAP expression) (P = 0.044). LNM number correlated positively with FTV (r = 0.474, P = 0.004) and TLF (r = 0.398, P = 0.018).

43058376.label: Conclusions
43058376.text: [18F]-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated comparable diagnostic accuracy to US for detecting primary thyroid lesions but offered superior pathological consistency for detecting cervical LNM. [18F]-FAPI -positive thyroid lesions exhibited a higher risk of ipsilateral cervical LNM. Furthermore, a higher FTV/TLF was associated with increased risk of LNM number, supporting the supplementary value of [18F]-FAPI PET/CT for preoperative staging and risk stratification in DTC.
